newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran court bans editor from press work for 10 years.
newsitem.headline: Iran court bans editor from press work for 10 years.

text.p: A court in Iran has banned a magazine editor from all journalistic work for 10 years for publishing an article that said Iranian universities were more Islamic than Moslem seminaries, a colleague said on Thursday.

The court in the holy city of Mashhad also fined Mohammad Sadeq Javadi Hessar, editor of the weekly Tous, three million rials ($1,000) after convicting him of causing public confusion and provoking antagonism between universities and seminaries, the magazine staff member told Reuters.

Javadi Hessar will appeal the ruling, which was based on lawsuits against the magazine over the article published in February, the colleague said. He spoke by telephone from Mashhad, 800 km (500 miles) east of Tehran.
"Most of our friends believe we are being pressured because Tous is the only paper that supports (presidential candidate Mohammad) Khatami in this region," he said.

Khatami, a former minister of culture and Islamic guidance, advocates more liberal cultural policies. He is one of the more prominent candidates who will face conservative Parliament Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri in the polls on May 23.

Javadi Hessar was sentenced in 1995 to 20 lashes and six months in jail on charges including slander after an earlier lawsuit against Tous, but the staff member said that conviction had been quashed on appeal. ($1=3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
